scope.summary: Rename the retained asupersync Cx driver family and its public Rust paths to oraclemcp-driver-cx without compatibility clones.
in_scope: Published package and library target identities for the driver, protocol, and derive crates
Generated FromRow paths and driver_cx derive helper attributes
Workspace consumers, tests, examples, benchmarks, CI, release scripts, SBOM, baselines, and current user documentation
Targeted exact-SHA compile, test, API-ledger, release-contract, and package-surface checks
out_of_scope: Uploading any renamed crate to crates.io
Live Oracle Database qualification and hosted Required CI
Repinning oraclemcp to the renamed family
Adding an Oracle driver backend or transferring legacy crates.io ownership

entry_points.name: Renamed driver package and public Rust crate
entry_points.trace: cargo clippy --all-targets, 348 default driver unit tests, 387 cassette-feature tests, 13 doctests, examples, benches, and pyshim compilation passed at source.sha.

entry_points.name: FromRow derive public surface
entry_points.trace: derive_trybuild passed both compile-pass fixtures and all five compile-fail fixtures using ::oraclemcp_driver_cx and #[driver_cx(...)].

entry_points.name: Release and package identity contracts
entry_points.trace: release_preflight, release_surface_manifest, secret_scan, cargo deny, gen_sbom, gen_baseline artifact diff, API ledger coverage of 3,763 lines, and single-path checks passed at source.sha.

limitations: The main crate registry-resolving package dry-run remains intentionally blocked until the renamed protocol and derive packages are published; rust-oracledb-cx-driver-handover-wgwq.4 owns that ordered transition.
This close does not claim live Oracle Database, hosted Required CI, crates.io visibility, or consumer-install evidence.
